text: 我就想问，为什么那么多回答写 卖淫合法后，就会出现大量的强迫卖淫和逼良为娼？
en: I just want to ask: why do so many answers claim that once prostitution is legalised, there will be a large amount of forced prostitution and coercion of decent women into prostitution?

text: 为什么那些黑社会在卖淫违法时不逼良为娼，要等到合法化才这样做？
en: Why is it that those gangsters do not force decent women into prostitution while prostitution is illegal, but wait until it is legalised to do so?

text: 如果逼良为娼一直存在，那和合不合法有什么直接关系？
en: If forcing decent women into prostitution has always existed, then what direct relation does it have with whether it is legal or not?

text: 国家对于卖淫场所的监管，对于黑社会限制人身自由，逼迫行为的打击，对于贩卖人口问题上的打击，在 卖淫合法后就不做了吗？
en: Does the state cease its regulation of prostitution venues, its crackdown on gangs restricting personal freedom and coercive conduct, and its crackdown on human trafficking, once prostitution is legalised?
2023.11.7 Additional supplement

text: 评论过多，补充下个人观点
en: Too many comments, so I will add some personal views.

text: 1 我知道现行的社会道德标准，不允许卖淫合法，所以我并不主张卖淫合法化。
en: 1 I know the current social moral standards do not permit prostitution to be legal, so I do not advocate the legalisation of prostitution.

text: 我也不讨论卖淫合化后，可能出现的道德问题和家庭问题。
en: Nor do I discuss the moral and family problems that might arise after prostitution is legalised.

text: 2 我反对卖淫合法会降低强奸率这个结论，我觉得两者并不相干。
en: 2 I oppose the conclusion that legalising prostitution would lower the rape rate; I think the two are not related.

text: 3 我只是非常反对其他回答中 卖淫合法化 后会出现大量的逼良为娼问题，我们可以就此展开讨论。
en: 3 I simply strongly object to the claim in other answers that legalising prostitution would lead to a large-scale problem of forcing decent women into prostitution; we can discuss this.

text: 4 目前我能想到的最合适的例子，现在KTV，酒吧的陪酒公主，是合法的工作吧，大家也会潜意识地认为她们的工作多多少少伴随着擦边和出卖肉体吧，我们可以讨论下她们更多的是自愿还是逼迫。
en: 4 The most fitting example I can think of: the 'drink princesses' who accompany patrons at KTVs and bars nowadays — that is legal work, is it not? And everyone subconsciously feels their work involves some borderline behaviour and selling their bodies, do they not? We can discuss whether more of them are there voluntarily or under coercion.

text: 我的观点是，我参考扫黄前东莞的盛状，在卖淫合化后，大量底层女性会自愿进入这行业，竞争变得激烈。
en: My view is, drawing on Dongguan's heyday before the anti-vice sweeps, that after prostitution is legalised large numbers of lower-class women would enter this industry voluntarily, and competition would become fierce.

text: 对于大型经营者来说，自愿女性的数量已经足够合法经营获得利润，不需要增加风险依靠黑社会或高利贷逼迫等违法行为。
en: For large operators, the number of voluntary women is already sufficient to run a legal business and make a profit; there is no need to take on added risk by relying on gangsters or loan sharks to coerce, which would be illegal conduct.

text: 竞争激烈也会导致利润降低，逼迫来的女性相对于自愿，需要支付更多的管理成本，并不划算。
en: Fierce competition would also lower profits; women who are coerced, compared with voluntary ones, require more management cost to be paid out, which is not cost-effective.

text: 当然，那些自愿女性基于社会道德原因，也不敢说自己从事这个行业，最终都是赚一笔快钱，然后上岸找个老实人嫁了。
en: Of course, those voluntary women, for reasons of social morality, also dare not say they are in this line of work; in the end they all make a quick buck, then leave the trade and marry an honest man.

text: 你反驳不了，因为现实中靠卖淫实现财务自由的妓女很多，而且现在这个社会氛围，明显也不是讲究贞洁被破了身子就要死要活的时代。
en: You cannot refute this, because in reality many prostitutes achieve financial freedom through prostitution, and the current social climate is clearly not an era that obsesses over chastity — that losing one's purity means wanting to die.

text: 而且妓女明显也不同情很多真底层民众，说不好听的，人家躺一晚上恐怕比你做一年视频挣得都多。
en: Moreover, prostitutes clearly do not sympathise with many truly bottom-rung people; to put it bluntly, lying down for one night probably earns them more than you would make from a year of making videos.

text: 你说人家是弱势群体？
en: You call them a vulnerable group?

text: 从上个世纪，抓卖淫团伙有组织有规模的，所谓真被逼良为娼的寥寥无几，反倒是用“生病的妈赌博的爸上学的弟弟”这套话术忽悠嫖客多掏钱的一抓一大把。
en: Since the last century, among the organised, large-scale prostitution gangs that have been caught, those genuinely forced from decency into prostitution are very few; on the contrary, those who use the spiel of 'a sick mother, a gambling father, a younger brother at school' to fool clients into paying more are caught in droves.

text: 而且注意了，这还是明面上的，不要忘了还有各种暗娼。
en: Besides, note that this is only the open, above-board side; do not forget there are also all sorts of underground prostitutes.

text: 如此氛围之下，你根本没有反驳的条件，不信你可以去问问你同情的那些所谓出来卖的失足妇女，有几个是真的家里穷的吃不上饭出来卖的？
en: Under such circumstances, you have no basis to refute at all. If you do not believe me, go and ask those so-called 'fallen women' who 'came out to sell' whom you pity — how many are truly so poor their family could not put food on the table and had to come out and sell themselves?

text: 波伏娃:免费不算卖
en: Beauvoir: for free does not count as selling.

text: 如果你认为贞洁是封建糟粕，性没什么神圣的，就和吃饭喝水一样，那为什么花钱请人做饭合法，花钱和人做爱非法？
en: If you believe chastity is feudal dross and sex is nothing sacred — just like eating and drinking — then why is paying someone to cook for you legal, but paying someone to have sex with you illegal?

text: 如果你认为性是神圣的，贞洁观念是必须的，那通奸、婚前性行为为什么不违法？
en: If you believe sex is sacred and the idea of chastity is necessary, then why are adultery and premarital sex not against the law?

text: 别扯什么强迫，“强迫卖淫”错在强迫，不在卖淫
en: Do not bring up coercion — 'forced prostitution' is wrong in the coercion, not in the prostitution.

text: 更别扯什么传染疾病，喘气还传染新冠呢，建议先立法禁止喘气
en: Do not even bring up disease transmission — breathing spreads Covid too, so I suggest legislating to ban breathing first.

text: 更新：有意思的是，评论区哈气的人一致认定我是支持*交易合法化
en: Update: interestingly, the people huffing in the comments section unanimously conclude that I support the legalisation of * transactions.

text: 但是只要具备基本的阅读理解能力，都能看懂我说的到底是什么
en: But anyone with basic reading comprehension can understand exactly what I am saying.

text: 借用高赞的说法，我反对的是包夜非法、包月包年合法，38.8万买断，但出了问题仅退货不退款模式
en: To borrow the wording of a top-voted comment: what I oppose is the model where an overnight arrangement is illegal but a monthly or yearly one is legal — a 388,000 buyout, yet when something goes wrong it is return-only, no-refund.

text: 要么全合法，要么全不合法。
en: Either make it all legal, or make none of it legal.

text: 这个话题下哈气的人一致质问：你敢不敢公开宣称⭐交易合法化、如果你老婆是⭐工作者你接不接受
en: Under this topic, the people huffing unanimously challenge me: would you dare publicly declare the legalisation of ⭐ transactions, and if your wife were a ⭐ worker, would you accept it?

text: 没有一个正面回答38.8万买断制算不算⭐交易
en: Not one of them directly answers whether the 388,000 buyout scheme counts as a ⭐ transaction.

text: 合法化的第一步是从语言上去污名化。
en: The first step in legalisation is to destigmatise it through language.

text: 什么叫“卖淫”呢？
en: What is meant by 'prostitution'?

text: 用钱换取性服务就叫“卖淫”吗？
en: Does exchanging money for sexual services count as 'prostitution'?

text: 那怎么不把约炮叫“自愿淫乱”，把结婚叫“长期淫乱”？
en: Then why not call casual hook-ups 'voluntary promiscuity' and marriage 'long-term promiscuity'?

text: 用钱换取的性服务有理由比自愿的和长期协定下的性关系更肮脏吗？
en: Is there any reason sexual services paid for with money should be dirtier than voluntary and long-term contractual sexual relationships?

text: 老实说我可以理解有些劳保把性神圣化的想法，但我唯独不懂某些伪劳保怎么只对性交易哈气？
en: Honestly, I can understand some labour-protectionists' notion of sanctifying sex, but the one thing I cannot grasp is why certain pseudo-labour-protectionists only huff at sex transactions?

text: 我不能理解为什么这种神圣性只会被市场化的交易亵渎而不会被非市场的交易，自愿的契约亵渎？
en: I cannot understand why this sacredness would be profaned only by marketised transactions and not by non-market transactions or voluntary contracts.

text: 既然花钱雇司机帮你开车不比你朋友帮你开车更肮脏，为什么花钱换取性服务就比自愿的性关系更肮脏呢？
en: Since paying a driver to drive for you is not dirtier than having a friend drive for you, why is paying for sexual services dirtier than a voluntary sexual relationship?

text: 平时都对法律百般不信，怎么到了卖淫这里又无比相信法律了？
en: Usually you distrust the law in every conceivable way; how come when it comes to prostitution you trust the law completely?

text: 选择性相信是吧？
en: Selective belief, is it?

text: 如何能保证从事性工作者所谓自愿的真实性？
en: How can we guarantee the authenticity of the so-called voluntariness of those who engage in sex work?

text: 发现评论区里很多人的要求是，一，要方便便宜的解决自己的需求，没有中间商赚差价。
en: I have found that many people in the comments want, first, to satisfy their own needs conveniently and cheaply, with no middleman taking a cut.

text: 二，要便捷的查询到从事过性工作者的身份，不能隐藏，以防结婚时娶错人╮（╯＿╰）╭
en: Second, to easily look up the identities of those who have done sex work, which must not be hidden, so as to avoid marrying the wrong person ╮（╯＿╰）╭

text: 设想一下如果合法化之后，张核子进军色情业可能会搞卖淫进校园
en: Imagine that after legalisation, Hezi Zhang enters the pornography industry and might push prostitution into school campuses.

text: 我记得罗翔说过这个问题。
en: I remember Xiang Luo spoke about this issue.

text: “卖淫合法”“买卖器官合法”实际上是一个问题，一旦承认合法，会造成强者对弱者的剥削。
en: 'Legalising prostitution' and 'legalising organ trading' are in fact one and the same issue; once legality is conceded, it creates exploitation of the weak by the strong.

text: 强者总有办法让你“被自愿”。
en: The strong always have ways to make you 'consent involuntarily'.

text: 如果我上小红书，对一个好看的姑娘说，你陪男人一晚上能挣1000块钱。
en: If I went on Xiaohongshu and said to a pretty girl, 'you could earn 1,000 yuan by keeping a man company for a night'.

text: 她会觉得被羞辱了，可能会举报让我封号。
en: She would feel humiliated and might report me to get my account banned.

text: 但如果我发个小红书，说姐妹们千万不要让男人白嫖啊。
en: But if I posted on Xiaohongshu saying, 'sisters, absolutely do not let men have it for free'.

text: 那我就是妥妥的女权主义者。
en: Then I would be a bona fide feminist.

text: 一些工作明显会导致尘肺，肺部永久损伤，无法恢复。
en: Some jobs clearly cause pneumoconiosis, permanent lung damage from which one cannot recover.

text: 这样的工作合法。
en: Such jobs are legal.

text: 一些工作明显会导致视力衰退，眼睛永久损伤，无法恢复。
en: Some jobs clearly cause deteriorating vision, permanent eye damage from which one cannot recover.

text: 这样的工作合法。
en: Such jobs are legal.

text: 一些工作风吹日晒明显会导致皮肤老化，这样的工作合法。
en: Some jobs, exposed to wind and sun, clearly cause skin ageing; such jobs are legal.

text: 一些工作导致血压血脂异常，体态异常，身心异常，这样的工作合法。
en: Some jobs cause abnormal blood pressure and blood lipids, abnormal posture, and abnormal physical and mental states; such jobs are legal.

text: 而性工作，绝大部分对身体没有明显损伤。
en: Yet sex work, in the vast majority of cases, causes no obvious harm to the body.

text: 都是工作，都是人的器官，都是主动选择，都是赚钱，凭什么你出卖肺、出卖眼睛、出卖手脚、出卖皮肤，就合法。
en: They are all work, all human organs, all active choices, all ways to earn money — on what grounds is it legal for you to sell your lungs, sell your eyes, sell your hands and feet, sell your skin?

text: 我出卖我的牛牛，菊花，生蚝...就不合法？
en: If I sell my willy, my anus, my oysters... that is not legal?

text: 如果说什么强迫行为，那请问中专生还没毕业就被学校卖到流水线上996，这是强迫吗？
en: If you are going to talk about coercive behaviour, then may I ask: when secondary-vocational students not yet graduated are sold by their school onto an assembly line for 996, is that coercion?

text: 怎么不禁止流水线工作？
en: Why not ban assembly-line work?

text: 所以，不合理的是“强迫本身”，而不是“工作”，能区分吗？
en: So what is unreasonable is 'coercion itself', not 'work' — can you tell the difference?

text: 卖淫能赚钱，所以强迫多。
en: Prostitution makes money, so there is more coercion.

text: 这也做不实。
en: This claim does not hold up either.

text: 流水线不赚钱吗？
en: Does not assembly-line work make money?

text: 不也有强迫的？
en: Are there not coercive cases there too?

text: 再说，为什么卖淫赚钱？
en: Furthermore, why does prostitution make money?

text: 因为这个市场是违法的，不是成熟的自由市场，资源稀缺。
en: Because this market is illegal, not a mature free market, and resources are scarce.

text: 如果是一个开放的、成熟的市场，有管理规范，还有天价b吗？
en: If it were an open, mature market with regulatory standards, would there still be sky-high b?

text: 还有天价丁吗？
en: Would there still be sky-high d?
